I looked for repeated nontrivial reasoning: the four Mel/Mmat_commute blocks in isCenter_vec, the ζ³=1 and σζ·ζ=1 preamble shared by isCenter_vec and isCenter_pair, the two branches in exists_move, exists_blk_a and exists_blk_b, and the projection argument in merge and isCenter_of_supp. Most of these are short, routine, or only a thin wrapper, so I did not report them. findings.problem: Both proofs show the same fact. Take the projection y = orthoEmb (F.blk a b) γ of v onto the 6-dimensional block, where γ i = herm σ (F.blk a b i) v. Then v - y is orthogonal to every blk vector. `merge` proves this as `hwblk`, via herm_sub_right, herm_blk_phi and simp. The zero case of `isCenter_of_supp` (lines 364–381) proves it again for the vectors F.f l a and F.f l b. It first rewrites them with exists_blk_a or exists_blk_b into blk i, then repeats `rw [hi, F.herm_blk_phi hab, hγ]; simp` twice, once for each of a and b. The orthogonality fact is never stated on its own, so each proof redoes the herm_blk_phi cancellation by hand.
findings.proposed_change: Add a lemma `herm_blk_sub_proj {a b : Fin m} (hab : a ≠ b) (v : Fin n → K) (i : Fin 6) : herm σ (F.blk a b i) (v - orthoEmb (F.blk a b) (fun j => herm σ (F.blk a b j) v)) = 0`. Proof sketch: `rw [herm_sub_right, F.herm_blk_phi hab]; simp`, which is exactly the body of `hwblk`. In `merge`, replace the `hwblk` block by `F.herm_blk_sub_proj hab v`. In `isCenter_of_supp`, replace the two branches s = a and s = b by `obtain ⟨i, hi⟩ := F.exists_blk_a s b l; rw [herm_sub_right] at *; ...` with `hi ▸ F.herm_blk_sub_proj hab v i`. Alternatively, state a second lemma `herm_f_sub_proj_a/b` that uses exists_blk_a/b once. The case s ∉ {a,b} stays as it is.
findings.benefit: The cancellation of the projection coefficient is stated and proved once. `merge` and `isCenter_of_supp` then read as "v - y is orthogonal to the block" plus the support bookkeeping. This removes the repeated `subst; obtain; rw [hi, herm_blk_phi, hγ]; simp` blocks. It also makes any later change to the definition of γ or blk a one-place edit.
